drivingQuestion: Is the rennet in the stomach of a carcass or of an animal slaughtered by a gentile forbidden, and may one curdle milk with it?
outcomeNote: Rav Ḥisda's answer is displaced by Rava's a fortiori and replaced by R' Yoḥanan's before/after the retraction; the unit closes with a fixed halakha permitting every rennet and forbidding only the stomach skin.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רֵישָׁא נִרְאֶה כְּאוֹכֵל נְבֵלוֹת, הָכָא אִיכָּא שְׁחִיטָה.
segments.en: «Rav Ḥisda said:» In fact, milk found in the stomach of a carcass is not itself prohibited. «The first clause» of the mishna prohibits it only because one who partakes of it «looks like one who eats carcasses,» which is repulsive. By contrast, «here,» with regard to a tereifa, the consumption of milk found in its stomach is less repulsive, as here «there is» at least «slaughter» of the animal.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְלָאו כֹּל דְּכֵן הוּא? וּמָה נְבֵלָה דִּמְאִיסָה, דְּאִי שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ קֵבָתָהּ לָא אָתֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינַּהּ, אָמְרַתְּ לָא. טְרֵפָה שְׁחוּטָה, דְּאִי שָׁרֵית אָתֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינַּהּ, לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
segments.en: «Rava said to» Rav Ḥisda: «But is it not» possible to claim «a fortiori» that milk found in the stomach of a tereifa should be prohibited? «Just as» with regard to «a carcass, which is» so «repulsive that» even «if you permit» the milk in «its stomach» people «will not come to partake of» the meat, «you» nevertheless «said» the milk is «not» permitted for consumption, is it «not all the more so» with regard to «a tereifa» that has been «slaughtered,» which is not as repulsive, «such that if you permit» the milk in its stomach people might «come to partake of it?»

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן קוֹדֶם חֲזָרָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר חֲזָרָה, וּמִשְׁנָה לֹא זָזָה מִמְּקוֹמָהּ.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Yitzḥak said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» This question is «not difficult.» The first clause of the mishna «here,» which teaches that the milk in the stomach of a carcass is prohibited, was taught «before» Rabbi Yehoshua’s «retraction» cited above, whereas the latter clause «there,» that milk from the stomach of a tereifa is permitted, was taught «after» Rabbi Yehoshua’s «retraction.» A mishna can sometimes preserve an older ruling and then immediately teach a contradictory later ruling, because «a mishna does not move from its place.» Since the first clause of the mishna was already canonized, it was not removed, despite Rabbi Yehoshua’s change of opinion.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַעֲמִידִין בְּקֵבַת נְבֵלוֹת, וְאֵין מַעֲמִידִין בְּקֵבַת שְׁחִיטַת גּוֹי. אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר סְתָם מַחְשֶׁבֶת גּוֹי לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
segments.en: § «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: One may curdle» milk «with» rennet extracted from «the stomach of carcasses, but one may not curdle» milk «with» rennet from «the stomach of» animals «slaughtered by a gentile. Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said before» Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: «In accordance with whose» opinion is this ruling? It is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer, who said: A gentile’s presumed intention» during slaughter «is for idol worship.» Therefore, the prohibition against deriving benefit from an animal slaughtered in idol worship applies to it, and this prohibition includes the contents of its stomach that are not actually part of its body. By contrast, a carcass is prohibited only for consumption, and the prohibition does not extend to the contents of its stomach.
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba «said to» Rabbi Shimon bar Abba: «Rather, in accordance with whose» opinion could this ruling be? Of course it is the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer.

segments.he: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַעֲמִידִין בֵּין בְּקֵבַת נְבֵלָה, בֵּין בְּקֵבַת שְׁחִיטַת גּוֹי, שֶׁלֹּא לָחוֹשׁ לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «When Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak came» from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, he said that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One may curdle» milk «both with» rennet from «the stomach of a carcass and with» rennet from «the stomach of» an animal «slaughtered by a gentile, as» there is «no» need «to be concerned for the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.» According to this account, Rabbi Yoḥanan does not maintain that a gentile’s presumed intention is for idol worship.

segments.he: וְהִלְכְתָא: אֵין מַעֲמִידִין בָּעוֹר קֵבַת נְבֵלָה, אֲבָל מַעֲמִידִין בְּקֵבַת נְבֵלָה, וּבְקֵבַת שְׁחִיטַת גּוֹי, וּבְקֵבַת כְּשֵׁרָה שֶׁיָּנְקָה מִן הַטְּרֵפָה, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן בְּקֵבַת טְרֵפָה שֶׁיָּנְקָה מִן הַכְּשֵׁרָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? חָלָב הַמְכוּנָּס בָּהּ פִּירְשָׁא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: «And» the «halakha» is: «One may not curdle» milk «with the skin of the stomach of a carcass, but one may curdle» milk «with» rennet from «the stomach of a carcass and with» rennet from «the stomach of» an animal «slaughtered by a gentile, and with» rennet from «the stomach of a kosher» animal «that suckled from a tereifa, and all the more so with» rennet from «the stomach of a tereifa» animal «that suckled from a kosher» animal. «What is the reason» for these lenient rulings? «The milk collected in» a stomach «is merely secretion» and is not considered food that can be prohibited.

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: רישא נראה כאוכל נבלות
moves.summary: answers the previous unit's contradiction: the first clause forbids only what looks like eating carcasses
moves.about: why the mishna's first clause forbids the rennet of a carcass although a tereifa's rennet is permitted

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא: ולאו כל דכן הוא?
moves.summary: Rava attacks by an a fortiori that would forbid the tereifa's rennet all the more
moves.about: whether an a fortiori from the repulsive carcass shows that the rennet of a slaughtered tereifa should be forbidden all the more

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רב יצחק, אמר רבי יוחנן: לא קשיא
moves.summary: replaces Rav Ḥisda's answer with R' Yoḥanan's: the clauses are from before and after the retraction
moves.about: Rav Yitzḥak reports R' Yoḥanan's resolution of the mishna's two clauses

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא, אמר רבי יוחנן: מעמידין בקבת נבלות
moves.summary: reports R' Yoḥanan permitting curdling with a carcass's rennet but not a gentile's slaughter
moves.about: R' Ḥiyya bar Abba reports R' Yoḥanan's ruling on curdling with rennet from a carcass and from a gentile's slaughter

moves.cueHe: אמר לפניו רבי שמעון בר אבא: כמאן?
moves.summary: asks whose view the ruling follows, and answers: R' Eliezer's
moves.about: whose opinion the ruling follows, given that it forbids only the rennet of a gentile's slaughter

moves.summary: confirms that the ruling can only follow R' Eliezer
moves.about: confirming the identification: in accordance with whose opinion else could the ruling be?

moves.cueHe: כי אתא רב שמואל בר רב יצחק, אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: brings a rival version of R' Yoḥanan's ruling, permitting both rennets
moves.about: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak brings from Eretz Yisrael a different version of R' Yoḥanan's ruling, permitting both rennets

moves.cueHe: והלכתא: אין מעמידין בעור קבת נבלה
moves.summary: fixes the halakha: only the stomach skin is forbidden, all the rennets are permitted
moves.about: the halakha follows the version of R' Yoḥanan that permits curdling with rennet from a carcass and from a gentile's slaughter, forbidding only the stomach skin

moves.summary: asks the reason for the lenient ruling
moves.about: the reason for these lenient rulings on rennet

moves.cueHe: חלב המכונס בה פירשא בעלמא הוא
moves.summary: answers that collected milk is mere secretion and not food
moves.about: the milk collected in the stomach is mere secretion and is not food that can become forbidden
